subject: Observability add-ons — retention/tracing/dashboard packaging and pricing
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Ellis <sarah.ellis@nimbusretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-02-11 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Observability add-ons — retention/tracing/dashboard packaging and pricing

Sarah — great to speak earlier. As discussed, I pulled together a concise matrix (attached) showing three options for observability add-ons that map to retention, tracing volume, and advanced dashboard seats. High-level items we want to confirm from your side so the quote is accurate: 

- Monthly active hosts / request volume (sample for peak hour vs steady-state)
- Expected 90-day vs 365-day retention needs for traces/logs
- Number of named dashboard seats and how many power users vs viewers

Attached: obs_pricing_matrix.xlsx and a SOW_template.pdf for timing notes. Proposed next steps: you share an estimate of 90-day trace volume and number of dashboards, I’ll refine the pricing tiers + a pilot offer for Q2.

Thanks,
Mike
Michael Grant
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Ellis <sarah.ellis@nimbusretail.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@nimbus-retail.com>, Amit Rao <amit.rao@nimbusretail.com>
Date: 2028-02-11 11:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons — retention/tracing/dashboard packaging and pricing

Mike — thanks for the summary and the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We expect ~120M trace events / month initially, trending to ~300M in 12 months if we roll out observability to all retail pipelines. Peak qps roughly 6x baseline.
- For compliance and investigations we need 180-day full trace retention for critical paths; 30-day for everything else.
- Dashboards: 8 power users, ~40 viewers across analytics and ops.
- Procurement asks about a volume discount and multi-year pricing — Amit is on copy to help with contracting cadence.

Can you sketch how the pilot would look (duration, what’s included) and what discount bands you can provide for a 12/24-month commit? Also confirm any egress/storage pass-throughs we should budget for.

—Sarah
Director, Observability — Nimbus Retail
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Ellis <sarah.ellis@nimbusretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-02-12 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons — retention/tracing/dashboard packaging and pricing

Sarah — great detail, very helpful. Based on your numbers I modeled three tailored packages (details in attached matrix):

1) Pilot (3 months): up to 150M traces total, 30-day default retention (option to tag + extend to 180d for up to 10% of traces), 4 dashboard seats (2 power). Flat pilot fee $18k (covers onboarding + two-week performance tuning).

2) Growth (12-month commit): up to 300M traces/month, 90-day standard retention, 8 power seats + 40 viewers, automated sampling on tail paths. Base price $22k/month. Discount bands: 10% at 12-month commit, 18% at 24-month commit. Includes prefix/KV cache improvements to reduce token cost for tracing ingestion.

3) Enterprise (24-month commit): unlimited traces within agreed-upon SLOs (we’ll set a cord for sustained qps), 180-day retention on critical traces, 12 power seats + 60 viewers, advanced dashboards SLA (1hr RTO for dashboard queries). Base price $38k/month. Discount bands: 18% at 24-month commit + crediting for long-term retention storage (we can provide storage credits for the first 6 months).

Notes on egress/storage: We include compressed archival storage for traces under the Enterprise plan without additional egress fees for queried restores up to 2TB/month. Anything above will be billed at cost; we can cap that as part of the SOW.

I’ve cc’d Marissa to validate technical assumptions and Ben for commercial terms. If you’re comfortable I’ll prepare a conditional SOW and a pricing PDF for procurement.

—Mike
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Ellis <sarah.ellis@nimbusretail.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-02-12 10:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons — retention/tracing/dashboard packaging and pricing

Sarah — quick note from the Solutions team: the 180-day retention on critical traces is feasible but we recommend tagging strategy to limit cost. Practical recommendations: 

- Tag 5–8 critical endpoints for full-fidelity retention; sample the rest at adaptive rates.
- Use trace-rollup (summaries) for 90–180 day windows to keep dashboard performance tight.
- For dashboards, seat-based concurrent limits will help control cost on high-cardinality queries.

I’ve started a short cost simulation in Drive (link above) with three scenarios using your 120M→300M ramp. Happy to run a joint session next week to walk the numbers and tune retention banding.

—Marissa
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Amit Rao <amit.rao@nimbusretail.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Sarah Ellis <sarah.ellis@nimbusretail.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@nimbus-retail.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-02-13 15:47:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons — retention/tracing/dashboard packaging and pricing

Team — thanks, this is the level of detail procurement needs. Quick responses and next steps from Nimbus: 

- We’ll start with a 3-month pilot targeted at checkout, cart, and search pipelines (approx 120M traces expected during pilot).
- Procurement prefers a capped pilot fee and a conditional credit toward the first month of a 12-month commit if we convert. The $18k flat pilot fee sounds reasonable if you can credit $8k toward the first invoice on conversion.
- For contract timeline: we need a draft SOW and a simple SLA appendix this week to route internally. Doc/DocuSign flow desired: internal review Feb 20, exec signoff Feb 28.

Can you send a draft SOW and a pricing PDF with the 12/24-month commit lines and the pilot-credit condition? We’ll aim to fast-track if the SOW shows the credit.

Regards,
Amit Rao
Head of Platform Partnerships — Nimbus Retail

Attachments referenced: nimbus_sow_draft.docx, pricing-final-20280211.pdf
